subject: POC environment handoff + MAP sequencing (API keys, org setup, safelist, peering)
messages:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@healthstack.io>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — POC checklist and who owns what

Thanks Mina — we want to lock the environment items this week so engineering can start provisioning. Can you confirm: 

- Who owns org setup (tenant + service account) vs. who sends API keys?
- Do you support VPC peering to our AWS account or just IP allowlist for trial?
- Any recommended TTL for ephemeral test keys during a two-week eval?

If you can share a short MAP with milestones and owners I can push to my infra lead.

Sophie
Sophie Grant
Director of Platform, HealthStack

Attachment: placeholder (we usually get a MAP spreadsheet)
From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@healthstack.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — POC checklist and who owns what

Hi Sophie — great to hear. Short answers up front, then a proposed MAP table below.

- Org setup: Redwood will create the Redwood tenant and seed the org-level service account (we own the control plane side). HealthStack does the cloud-side IAM binding for the service account in your AWS account. Owner: Redwood (org seed) / HealthStack infra (IAM bind).
- API keys: Redwood issues ephemeral API keys for the eval. We can issue 2-week keys scoped to the test tenant. Owner: Redwood (provision) / HealthStack (apply key to test clients).
- Connectivity: We support both IP allowlist (quick) and VPC peering (preferred for longer trials). For a fast start, do IP allowlist and we’ll run a parallel peering-ticket to get peering ready.

Proposed MAP milestones (high-level):
1) Day 0–1: Org seed + initial API keys (Redwood)
2) Day 1–3: HealthStack IAM binding + test token usage (HealthStack)
3) Day 3–7: IP allowlist validation + smoke tests (joint)
4) Day 4–14: VPC peering runbook / peering window (parallel)
5) Day 10–14: Performance sanity & telemetry baseline (joint)

I’m attaching a concise MAP spreadsheet and a simple network handshake diagram. Can you confirm who on your side will be the peering contact (account id + infra owner email)? Once we have that we’ll open the peering ticket and a DocuSign MAP for signatures.

Mini-asks: please share your AWS account id and a contact for peering by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Karthik for any runtime/quant profiles in case you want specific batch/latency targets.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
M: +1 (415) 555-0118

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx, network_handshake_diagram.pdf

Date: 2026-10-22T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: who will own each MAP line item

Quick internal note — assigning owners so we have a single point per action: 

- Org seed + API key creation: Mina (owner)
- Peering ticket + infra coordination: Jonas (owner)
- Network validation & allowlist review: Marissa (owner)
- Runtime tuning / quant suggestions: Karthik (owner)
- Contract signature / DocuSign: Sales Ops (loop if needed)

Target timeline: start tomorrow (10/23). If HealthStack provides account id and peering contact by 10/23 17:00 PT we can have peering request in the queue the next day. Otherwise we default to IP allowlist to avoid blocking.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Engagement Manager, Redwood Inference

Replying to include our preferred peering template and the short MAP we will send externally. Put both in the drive folder after Mina sends to the customer.
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-23T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: who will own each MAP line item

Sounds good. A couple implementation notes for the peering path: 
- For HealthStack’s AWS account we’ll request VPC id, region, and the peering admin email. We’ll provide a small CloudFormation snippet to create the route entry on their side (minimizes back and forth).
- Security Q: if they want to skip peering and rely on allowlist only, confirm they accept TLS + signed audit headers for request tracing.
- For ephemeral keys: recommend 14-day TTL with a refresh endpoint we manage; if they want shorter we can do 48-hour rolling keys for CI tests.

I’ll draft the peering ticket once they share account id. Karthik — flag anything runtime-wise we should pre-seed in the MAP: model size, expected concurrent calls, latency SLOs.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

- VPC peering ticket (Jonas) — open by 2026-10-29, expected window 5–7 business days

3) Sign the short MAP (DocuSign link attached) to approve the onboarding plan and SLAs.
